newsitem.title: RUSSIA: TENNIS-RUSSIANS START KREMLIN CUP IN WINNING STYLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUSSIANS START KREMLIN CUP IN WINNING STYLE.

text.p: Russia's Elena Makarova upstaged sixth seed Silvia Farina in the first round of the Kremlin Cup women's tournament on Monday from which Steffi Graf was forced to pull out through injury.
Makarova's 5-7 6-4 6-2 win over the Italian, ranked 37th in the world, made her one of two Russians to advance to the second round.
The other was emerging 16-year-old talent Anna Kournikova, who needed less than an hour to beat German Elena Wagner 6-0 6-4.
Austrian players also made a strong start, with Sandra Dopfer accounting for Korea's Sung-Hee Park 6-1 6-4 and seventh seed Barbara Schett beating Rita Grande of Italy 6-4 6-3.

The organisers of the $400,000 tournament confirmed on Sunday that Graf would be unable to compete, but said she would visit Moscow for two days to conduct a tennis class and possibly take on Kournikova in an exhibition match.
